title: Minneapolis with Clarence Johnson and meeting Bill Pugh
summary: Thomas moves to the Twin Cities to play with pianist Clarence Johnson, who could not read; he recalls a trumpeter hired by Trent just for blues and Hinton's tie to Bill Pugh.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: But then, I had to keep studying. So I went from Minot to Minneapolis. Now, I don't exactly how I got to... I guess maybe I got to Minneapolis through Art Graham. But that was really the beginning of my career. Because I went there and played with a guy named Clarence Johnson. Now, Clarence didn't read, but he had good ear. His wife could teach him the music...
What did he play?
He played piano. He was a good piano player, too, but he just couldn't read. But he... You know... Did you ever come across one of them piano players who was good but couldn't read?
Oh, sure!

Of course, thinking of that, we had a trumpet player from Oklahoma; this cat couldn't read a note as big as a house. But Alphonso Trent hired him just to play the Blues. He could play the Blues! He could play the Blues,
Thomas - 41

and he could play it in different keys, too.
So I joined Clarence Johnson, and he had a little thing... It was a little better, because we was in the Twin Cities, in Minneapolis and St. Paul... And that's where I met Pugh. Remember I used to talk to you about Pugh?
Bill Pugh.
Yeah. That's where I first met him.
Yeah! Well, I remember when I was a paper boy, I met him in Chicago.
I don't know whether I met him in Minneapolis... He wasn't out in that Wild West country. So...
That's the funniest. Here we've got Bill Pugh, and he was on his way to be a good-looking cat and a pimp.
He was a handsome guy.
Yes.
He was a handsome guy. He turned out to be a pimp.
He came... We saw him in New York. He came to all ...(?)...
Yeah. Right. Yeah!
He was so proud of me after I got with the band, because I used to be his newspaper boy in Chicago.
Thomas - 42
Right, he told me that. That's how I knew that you knew him.
That's beautiful. I remember that story, Foots.
Yeah, I remember that. So now, let me get on with Minneapolis.
